subject: mcc-health-promotion
title: Cervical cancer screening: key decisions in primary care

steps.tx: A woman with **HPV 16** needs direct evaluation even when cytology is normal. HPV 16 is strongly linked to high-grade lesions. Viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 inactivate p53 and Rb, driving progressive dysplasia. Cytology samples surface cells and can miss lesions, so a normal smear does not exclude CIN2 or CIN3. Colposcopy with biopsy is the appropriate next step.
steps.say: A woman with HPV 16 needs direct evaluation even when her cytology is normal. HPV 16 is strongly linked to high grade lesions. Viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 inactivate p53 and Rb, driving progressive dysplasia. Cytology samples surface cells and can miss lesions, so a normal smear does not exclude CIN2 or CIN3. steps.tx: Screening is only indicated while the cervix is present and the woman is within the screening age range. A **total hysterectomy** performed for benign disease, with no history of CIN2 or higher and no cervical cancer, removes the target organ. Routine screening can therefore stop. Women with prior high-grade disease or cancer need continued follow-up, so the history must be checked first.

steps.tx: Pregnancy changes the timing of treatment. Biopsy-confirmed **CIN2 or CIN3** without suspicion of invasion is usually managed by surveillance during pregnancy, because excision carries risks of bleeding and preterm birth. Suspected invasion needs urgent imaging and specialist input. Treatment is generally deferred to the postpartum period, with colposcopic surveillance in between.

steps.tx: Overdue women can be reached with **self-collected HPV testing**, which performs comparably to clinician-collected samples. Fear of speculum examination and transport barriers are addressed by this approach, supported by navigation help. Concurrent anaemia needs its own work-up and should not delay screening. Vaccination lowers risk but does not replace screening, because vaccine types do not cover all oncogenic HPV.

steps.tx: Biopsy-confirmed **CIN2** at the transformation zone in a woman who has completed her family is best treated by excision. The **loop electrosurgical excision procedure** removes the transformation zone and allows histological assessment of margins. Observation with follow-up is reserved for selected cases, and hysterectomy is not first line. HIV and hepatitis C results do not change this choice.
